description: Entering the sign-up code with a different email than the one the code was sent for used up the code, so the customer had to ask for a new one.
steps: 1. Request a sign-up code for email A. 2. Submit the form with email B and the code. 3. Submit again with email A and the same code.
expected: Step 2 refused; the code still works in step 3.
actual: Step 3 failed with "Ask for a code first".
root_cause: The code was deleted before the email check ran.
fix: verifyOtp() now runs the email check before consuming the code (server/src/lib/otp.js).

description: If a customer paid online after the order had been cancelled, the payment was marked confirmed but no refund was opened; the gateway checkout could also be started for a cancelled order.
steps: 1. Place an order. 2. Cancel it. 3. Start online payment and complete it (or the gateway webhook arrives late).
expected: Payment cannot start for a cancelled order; a late payment opens a full refund automatically.
actual: Payment started; money taken; no refund record; nothing ships.
root_cause: confirmGatewayPayment() and /payments/gateway/create did not check the order status.
fix: Gateway create refuses cancelled orders (409). A payment that arrives after cancellation opens a full refund (paymentAfterCancel in lib/returns.js) and is not sent to a dealer.
retest: PARTIAL — API refuses payment on cancelled orders (CUS-CAN-004). The late-webhook path needs a Razorpay sandbox test once keys are configured.

description: One-time codes (sign-up, password reset, dealer signing) and the 4-digit delivery code were saved in plain text in the notifications table.
steps: Request any code, then read the notifications table.
expected: Stored copy does not contain the code.
root_cause: The outbox stored the exact text that was sent.
fix: notifyContact()/notifyOrder() store a masked copy (••••••); only the message sent contains the code.

description: The admin order list showed only the newest 500 orders with no paging, so older orders could only be found by search, and every row loaded full order details.
steps: Have more than 500 orders; open Admin → Orders.
expected: Paged list with a total count.
fix: ?limit & ?page with X-Total-Count; the page loads 100 at a time with "Show 100 more".
retest: PASS (PERF-003: 3,004 orders, 82 ms per page; PERF-004)

description: Deleting the default address left the customer with no default address; deleting an address id that belongs to someone else returned OK (nothing was deleted, but no error).
steps: 1. Have two addresses. 2. Delete the default one.
expected: The other address becomes default; foreign ids give 404.
root_cause: DELETE did not reassign the default or check ownership before answering.
fix: Ownership check (404), default moves to the newest remaining address; edit and set-default endpoints added.

description: The same mobile number could be used on several customer accounts (at sign-up and in My Profile).
steps: Register account A with 98xxxxxx01; register account B (different email) with the same mobile.
fix: Mobile number checked at code request, sign-up and profile update (409).

description: A dealer could create two products with the same SKU.
steps: Add two products with SKU GDH-PC-01.
fix: SKU must be unique per dealer (409 with a field message) on create and edit.

description: The new Finance Admin role could not confirm or reject payments, because the payment action is sent to the orders endpoint, which Finance may only view.
steps: Sign in as Finance Admin; confirm a payment.
actual: 403 "Your role can view this page but cannot make changes."
root_cause: Area map looked only at the URL path.
fix: Payment decisions on /orders/:id/action are treated as the Payments area in the permission gate.

description: A malformed JSON body or a body over 200 KB returned the raw parser message (e.g. "Unexpected token } in JSON at position 11").
steps: POST invalid JSON to any endpoint.
root_cause: Body-parser errors were passed through with their own message.
fix: errorHandler maps parse/size errors to friendly messages and never echoes non-application error text.

description: A double tap on "Place Order" or a retry after a dropped connection could create two orders and take stock twice.
steps: Send the same order twice at the same moment.
fix: Checkout sends an Idempotency-Key per attempt; the server returns the same order for a repeated key (24 h). The button is also locked while placing.

description: Status badges (warning/OK colours), manual chapter numbers and callout circles had too little colour contrast; admin dashboard chart bars used ARIA labels that are not allowed inside an image; scrollable tables could not be reached with the keyboard; the Returns filter used a tab list without tabs.
steps: Run axe-core (WCAG 2 A/AA) on the pages.
actual: Up to 80 issues per page (admin products).
fix: Darker status colours, manual colours, role fixes, tables focusable with a label.

description: The Security page scrolled sideways on desktop (62 px) and phones (226 px).
steps: Open Admin → Security at 1366 px and 412 px.
root_cause: Tables outside a scroll wrapper and a grid column using 1fr (minimum = content width).

page: Empty cart, checkout, policy page, dealer orders
description: Some pages had no main heading (h1), which hurts screen-reader navigation and SEO.
root_cause: Empty states used h3; policy page title came from the document body.
fix: Empty states can render an h1; hidden h1 on policy and dealer order pages.

description: Opening the dealer sign-in page logged a 401 error in the browser console.
root_cause: The first session check returned 401 when signed out.
fix: /dealer/me?soft=1 answers 200 { dealer: null } when there is no session cookie.

description: On phones the "Deals & festival alerts" card opened over the product page and covered the "Add to Cart" button.
steps: On a phone, view 2 products; on the second the card appears after 4 s.
expected: The buy button is never covered.
actual: Card covered Add to Cart until closed.
root_cause: Card shown on all non-checkout pages at full width on phones.
fix: Not shown on phone product pages or account, dealer, help and tracking pages.

description: On first start the seed script printed the admin email AND password to the server log. On a hosting platform this puts the admin password in the deploy logs.
steps: Deploy with ADMIN_PASSWORD set; open the service logs.
expected: Log names the admin email only.
root_cause: Developer convenience message left in seed.js.
fix: The message now says the password comes from ADMIN_PASSWORD and must be changed at first sign-in; no password is printed. A test checks the start-up log for the password and secrets.
